issues.legal_issue: A claimant’s right to obtain a reference and the authority’s power to make one end when the claimant fails to seek a court direction within the applicable limitation period after the authority misses its deadline.
material_facts: Claimants in the appeals had sought references, but the authority did not make them within the prescribed period.
Some claimants applied to court to compel references only after the limitation period had expired.
In one matter, the High Court held that the authority could still make a reference after the claimant’s time to seek a court direction had run out.
issues.conclusion: Once the claimant’s time to seek a court direction expires, the claimant’s remedy and the authority’s power to make the reference both end; a reference made afterward is incompetent.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 18(2) and Section 18(3)(a)–(b) of the Land Acquisition Act as amended in Karnataka, a claimant must apply for a reference within the prescribed period, the authority must act within 90 days, and the claimant must apply to court within the limitation period under Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963. Thakoredas establishes the applicable limitation period. Reading the provisions harmoniously, the statutory scheme and its purpose of preventing stale or belated claims imply that the remedy and the authority’s power end together. The Court approved the reasoning in Special Land Acquisition Officer v. G.C. Paramraj and Assistant Commissioner v. Laxmi Bai, and distinguished the scheme under the unamended Central Act.

predicates.compel_reference_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a claimant seeking to compel an authority to send a compensation claim to a court for determination.
predicates.timely_reference_request: The claimant submitted the initial request for a reference within the applicable time limit.
predicates.authority_failed_to_refer_within_its_dea: The authority did not send the claim to court within the period allowed for doing so.
predicates.claimant_failed_to_seek_court_direction_: The claimant did not apply to court for a direction before the applicable limitation period expired.

issues.definition: When a claimant timely requests a reference, the authority misses its deadline, and the claimant does not seek a court direction in time, both the claimant’s remedy and the authority’s power to make the reference end.

issues.legal_issue: The general power to extend time for delay cannot be used to revive an expired right to seek a court direction compelling a reference.
material_facts: Some claimants applied to court to compel references after the applicable limitation period had expired.
Claimants sought condonation of delay, including after delays of many years.
The courts below had treated the general delay-condonation provision as available for these applications.
issues.conclusion: A claimant cannot invoke Section 5 of the Limitation Act to condone delay in an application to court under the Karnataka-amended reference scheme; an out-of-time application must be dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Article 137 of the Limitation Act applies to an application to court to compel a reference, as held in Thakoredas. Under the Karnataka-amended Section 18 scheme, expiry of the limitation period ends the remedy to obtain a reference, so Section 5 cannot revive it. The Court relied also on Officer on Special Duty (Land Acquisition) v. Shah Manilal Chandulal for the inapplicability of Section 5 in proceedings before the land-acquisition authority.

predicates.compel_reference_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an application to court to compel an authority to send a compensation claim for judicial determination.
predicates.court_application_filed_after_limitation: The claimant filed the application to court after the applicable limitation period had expired.
predicates.claimant_sought_delay_condonation: The claimant asked the court to excuse the late filing.

issues.definition: If a claimant applies out of time to compel a reference and asks for delay to be excused, the expired reference remedy cannot be revived by condoning the delay.

issues.legal_issue: A late initial application seeking a reference cannot be extended by applying the general statutory power to condone delay in proceedings before the land-acquisition authority.
material_facts: Some claimants made their initial applications for references after the period prescribed for seeking them had expired.
The State argued that Section 5 of the Limitation Act did not apply to those applications.
The Court held that an initial application for a reference must be made within the time fixed by the Karnataka amendment.
issues.conclusion: Section 5 of the Limitation Act cannot be used to extend the time for an initial application seeking a reference before the land-acquisition authority.
issues.legal_principle: Section 18(2) of the Land Acquisition Act as amended in Karnataka requires the initial application to be made within the prescribed 90-day period. Shah Manilal holds that Section 5 of the Limitation Act does not apply to proceedings before the land-acquisition authority; the application must therefore comply with the statutory time limit.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_claim: The proceeding concerns a claim for compensation for acquired land and a request for a reference for determination of that claim.
predicates.initial_reference_request_filed_after_st: The claimant submitted the initial request for a reference after the applicable statutory filing period had expired.

issues.definition: If an initial reference request in a land-acquisition compensation claim is filed after the statutory window, delay cannot be condoned to save it.
